title: Ghost in the Layers
story:
From: Tomasz Wierzba
Subject: URGENT, a password I deleted is still there

The legacy image `kestrel/legacy-archive:0.9` was built years ago. Its Dockerfile copied in a credentials file and then ran `rm` on it in the next step, so I assumed the password was gone. Wren's predecessor says it is not. Prove it.

Recover the archive password from the image's layers and write it to `/workspace/recovered.txt`. The original source folder was deleted, so you only have the image. Then build a clean `kestrel/archive-clean:1.0` from `alpine:3.20` that ships `/workspace/index.txt` as `/srv/archive/index.txt`, with no trace of the password in any layer.
objectives: Recover the archive password (the `ARCHIVE_PASSWORD` value) from the layers of `kestrel/legacy-archive:0.9` and write it to `/workspace/recovered.txt`
The clean image must have no password file and no trace of the password in its history
startingState: The image `kestrel/legacy-archive:0.9` exists locally. `/workspace/index.txt` is the new archive index. The old build folder no longer exists.
hints: A deleted file is only hidden by a newer layer. The earlier layer that added it is still stored inside the image, and `docker history` lists the steps that created each layer.

Export the image with `docker save IMAGE -o file.tar` and unpack it with `tar`. Every layer is a gzipped tarball under `blobs/`; list their contents with `tar -tzf` until you find the file that `docker history` shows being copied in, then extract just that file to stdout. For the clean image, never copy the credentials file in at all.

```bash
docker history --no-trunc kestrel/legacy-archive:0.9
docker save kestrel/legacy-archive:0.9 -o legacy.tar
mkdir -p x && tar -xf legacy.tar -C x
for b in x/blobs/sha256/*; do tar -tzf $b 2>/dev/null | grep -q archive.cred && tar -xzOf $b etc/archive.cred; done
# write the password value to recovered.txt, then build an image from FROM + COPY index.txt only
```

commands:
mkdir -p /tmp/legacy-build && cd /tmp/legacy-build && printf 'ARCHIVE_PASSWORD=Borealis-7714-Tern
' > archive.cred && printf 'FROM alpine:3.20
COPY archive.cred /etc/archive.cred
RUN rm /etc/archive.cred
CMD ["echo", "archive ready"]
' > Dockerfile && docker build -q -t kestrel/legacy-archive:0.9 . && cd / && rm -rf /tmp/legacy-build

validation.description: The clean image's history never mentions the credentials

solution: docker save kestrel/legacy-archive:0.9 -o /tmp/legacy.tar && mkdir -p /tmp/x && tar -xf /tmp/legacy.tar -C /tmp/x && for b in /tmp/x/blobs/sha256/*; do tar -tzf $b 2>/dev/null | grep -q archive.cred && tar -xzOf $b etc/archive.cred; done | sed 's/ARCHIVE_PASSWORD=//' > recovered.txt; cat recovered.txt
debrief: Image layers are append-only: deleting a file in a later layer only hides it, and anyone with the image can pull it back out. Pro tip: never COPY a secret into a build, and if you must use one, use a BuildKit secret mount so it never lands in a layer.
